title: Firstfruits: The Harvest That Reveals Who Owns Your Heart
paragraphs:
Firstfruits: The Harvest That Reveals Who Owns Your Heart
Before God Asked for the Harvest, He Asked for Trust
There is a question hidden beneath every blessing God places in our hands.
It is not how much we have.
It is not how successful we become.
It is not how large the harvest grows.
The question is this:
Who receives the first and best portion?
That question sits at the center of one of the most misunderstood biblical concepts in all of Scripture: Firstfruits.

Many people reduce firstfruits to a financial principle. Others treat it as an Old Testament agricultural custom that no longer matters. But when we journey into the Scriptures and examine the original languages, historical context, and the unfolding story of redemption, we discover something far deeper.
Firstfruits is not ultimately about crops.
It is about worship.
It is about trust.
It is about surrender.
It is about whether God is truly first.
And if we are honest, that question exposes every one of us.
Because most of us do not struggle to give God what is left.
We struggle to give Him what is first.

The Hebrew word translated "firstfruits" is רֵאשִׁית (reshith). It carries the idea of the beginning, the chief part, the first and best portion. It comes from a root connected to "head" or "first place."
God was never asking Israel for leftovers.
He was asking for the portion that represented everything else.
The first bundle of grain.
The first ripe fruit.
The first increase.
The firstborn.
The first and best.
Because the first portion revealed what people believed about the Giver.
This is why Proverbs 3:9–10 declares:
"Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your produce; then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will be bursting with wine."
Notice the order.
Honor comes before abundance.
Trust comes before increase.
Worship comes before blessing.
Firstfruits was never a transaction.
It was a declaration.
It was saying:
"God, before I know how large the harvest will be, I trust You."
That changes everything.
Because giving after abundance requires gratitude.
Giving before abundance requires faith.
And faith has always been the language God understands.
This becomes even more powerful when we understand Israel's agricultural reality.
The firstfruits offering was brought before the full harvest arrived.
The farmer had not yet seen the final outcome.
Storms could still come.
Drought could still happen.
Locusts could still destroy everything.
Yet God commanded His people to bring the first portion anyway.
Why?
Because firstfruits transformed fear into worship.
It was a public declaration that God's faithfulness mattered more than visible security.
How many of us are still waiting for certainty before obeying God?
How many of us tell ourselves we will trust Him after everything becomes safe?
But biblical faith has never operated that way.
Faith steps forward before the evidence arrives.
Faith obeys before the outcome is visible.
Faith gives God the first portion because faith knows the harvest belongs to Him already.
Yet the story of firstfruits becomes even more breathtaking when we move beyond agriculture and into the Gospel itself.
Because the greatest firstfruits offering in history was not grain.
It was Jesus Christ.
When Paul writes in 1 Corinthians 15:20, he says:
The Greek word used here is ἀπαρχή (aparche).
Paul intentionally connects Christ's resurrection to the firstfruits offering.
Jesus rose first.
Not last.
First.
His resurrection became God's guarantee that everyone who belongs to Him will also be raised.
The empty tomb was Heaven's firstfruits offering to humanity.
One resurrected Savior guaranteeing a coming harvest of redeemed people.
Think about that.
The stone rolled away.
The grave surrendered.
Death lost its grip.
And Christ emerged as the firstfruits of a future resurrection harvest that cannot fail.
This is why the doctrine of firstfruits is not ultimately about money.
It is about Jesus.
Everything in Scripture points toward Him.
The fields pointed toward Him.
The offerings pointed toward Him.
The feasts pointed toward Him.
The sacrifices pointed toward Him.
The firstfruits pointed toward Him.
And then something even more astonishing happens.
God does not merely ask for firstfruits.
God gives firstfruits.
John 3:16 tells us:
"For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son."
The Father gave His first and best.
Before humanity deserved it.
Before repentance occurred.
Before righteousness existed.
Before we cleaned ourselves up.
Before we came home.
He gave.
The Gospel begins with God offering His Firstfruits to save rebels.
That changes how we see every act of surrender.
Because Christianity is never us giving something to convince God to love us.
It is us responding to the love already demonstrated through Christ.
And that is where many of us find ourselves today.
We carry shame from old failures.
Regret from old decisions.
Scars from broken relationships.
Secrets nobody knows.
We wonder whether God could still use someone like us.
Whether our story has gone too far.
Whether the harvest is already ruined.
But the Gospel has always been a story of firstfruits emerging from broken ground.
A shepherd becomes a king.
A persecutor becomes an apostle.
A prostitute becomes part of the Messiah's lineage.
A thief enters paradise.
A cross becomes a throne.
An empty tomb changes history.
This is what God does.
He specializes in rewriting stories.
He takes scandal and produces grace.
He takes failure and produces redemption.
He takes ashes and produces beauty.
He takes dead things and brings them back to life.
That is why firstfruits is ultimately about more than giving.
It is about lordship.
Who gets first place?
Who receives the first affection?
The first trust?
The first devotion?
The first obedience?
Because whatever receives first place eventually shapes everything else.
Jesus said in Matthew 6:33:
"Seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added to you."
The kingdom first.
Christ first.
The Gospel first.
Not because God needs our resources.
Because He wants our hearts.
And hearts are always revealed by what comes first.
Maybe that is why this message feels personal.
Because every reader is standing somewhere in a field.
Holding something valuable.
A dream.
A relationship.
A career.
A future.
A gift.
A calling.
A burden.
A wound.
And God is gently asking the same question He has asked throughout Scripture:
"Will you trust Me with the first and best?"
Not because He wants to take from you.
Because He wants to show you that He is enough.
Maybe today is the day you stop giving God leftovers.
Maybe today is the day Christ becomes first again.
Maybe today is the day your harvest begins with surrender.
And maybe someone reading this needed this reminder more than you realize.
Your testimony may become someone else's encouragement.
Because the greatest Firstfruits offering was never grain placed on an altar.
It was a Savior stretched upon a cross.
And because He rose, your story is not finished.
The harvest is still coming.
The tomb is still empty.
And grace is still rewriting lives.
The same God who received the firstfruits is still producing miracles from surrendered hearts.
What you place first today reveals what you believe about eternity tomorrow.
